about: vowel, a formant filter that makes any sound say a, e, i, o, u: a level-8 effect (docs/level-8.md) in the unit's own lists of effects, for a sound (shift and T3) and for the master (the mixer's list), and on fx train's wagons. It stands on the unit's cwo: a sound saved with it keeps cwo's name and four knobs, switched off, and plays dry on a unit without the pack. Its four values on the knobs and the LFOs: vowel, shift, motion (envelope or a tempo-locked sweep from the block's period), mix. Shift + blue turns RES and shift + red LEVEL on its page, kept as the level-7 member vowel_layer with the synth's and drum's sounds and the master. A small working memory for each place, cleared at fresh. T3 shows its page, its own picture vowel-face.svg standing in for the effect's page: a head whose lips, jaw and tongue say the vowel, smaller and with the larynx higher as shift rises, a vowel chart, the motion at the throat and the mix as sound lines and a meter, dressed with the values as the sound plays them (level 10); without the picture it paints them on the base's blank page. It changes no place of the firmware, names no address of it and needs the base (level 10).
name: vowel
